hook.line: Written Spanish and formal speech love to pack a reason or a time into a few words at the start of the sentence. Once you spot the pattern, you read faster and you sound more polished.
hook.es: Terminado el trabajo, Tomás cerró el café.
hook.en: Once the work was finished, Tomás closed the café.

examples.es: Construido en 1920, el edificio sigue en pie.
examples.en: Built in 1920, the building is still standing.

examples.es: Siendo tan tarde, preferimos tomar un taxi.
examples.en: Since it's so late, we'd rather take a taxi.

examples.es: Terminado el trabajo, Tomás cerró el café.
examples.en: Once the work was finished, Tomás closed the café.

examples.es: Sabiendo que Altamira quiere comprar, Tomás no firmó.
examples.en: Knowing that Altamira wants to buy, Tomás didn't sign.

examples.es: Cerrado el café, Vale se fue a casa.
examples.en: With the café closed, Vale went home.

examples.es: Abierto desde 1950, el café tiene muchos clientes.
examples.en: Open since 1950, the café has many customers.

rule:
Instead of a full clause with *porque* or *cuando*, you can open the sentence with a participle (*-ado*, *-ido*) or a gerund (*-ando*, *-iendo*), then a comma, then the main clause.

Participle: something already done or a state. It agrees with its noun: *Construido en 1920*, *Cerrada la puerta*, *Terminado el trabajo*.

Gerund: a reason or a condition at the same time: *Siendo tarde…*, *Sabiendo que…*.

The opening part usually shares the subject of the main clause, or has its own noun right after it (*Terminado el trabajo*).

Never use the gerund for something that happens afterwards.
smallPrint: Teachers call these participial and gerund clauses; with their own noun (*Terminado el trabajo*) they are called absolute constructions.

readAndPick.es: Construido en 1920, el edificio sigue en pie.
options: Built in 1920, the building is still standing.
Building in 1920, the building is still standing.
It will be built in 1920, and the building will stand.

readAndPick.es: Siendo tan tarde, preferimos tomar un taxi.
options: Although it's late, we'd rather take a taxi.
Since it's so late, we'd rather take a taxi.
When it's late, we always take a taxi.

readAndPick.es: Terminado el trabajo, Tomás cerró el café.
options: While finishing the work, Tomás closed the café.
Before finishing the work, Tomás closed the café.
Once the work was finished, Tomás closed the café.

readAndPick.es: Sabiendo que Altamira quiere comprar, Tomás no firmó.
options: Knowing that Altamira wants to buy, Tomás didn't sign.
Altamira knew that Tomás didn't sign.
Wanting to buy, Altamira didn't sign.

readAndPick.es: Cerrado el café, Vale se fue a casa.
options: With the café open, Vale went home.
With the café closed, Vale went home.
Closing the café, Vale went home.

readAndPick.es: Abierto desde 1950, el café tiene muchos clientes.
options: Opening in 1950, the café will have many customers.
Closed since 1950, the café has many customers.
Open since 1950, the café has many customers.

readAndPick.es: Siendo extranjero, Tomás no conocía la ciudad.
options: Being a foreigner, Tomás didn't know the city.
Tomás, a local, knew the city.
Tomás doesn't know the foreigner.

readAndPick.es: Pintada de azul, la casa se ve más grande.
options: Painting blue, the house looks bigger.
Painted blue, the house looks bigger.
It will be painted blue, and the house will look bigger.

readAndPick.es: Conociendo a Don Hernando, va a llegar tarde.
options: Knowing Don Hernando, he'll arrive late.
Don Hernando knows him, so he arrived late.
Don Hernando will meet him late.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *Construido* or *Construida* and type the whole sentence: *___ en 1920, el edificio sigue en pie.*
yourTurn.answer: Construido en 1920, el edificio sigue en pie.
yourTurn.why: The participle agrees with *edificio*, which is masculine.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Since it's so late, we'd rather take a taxi.
yourTurn.answer: Siendo tan tarde, preferimos tomar un taxi.
yourTurn.why: *Siendo* gives the reason in two words.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Once the work was finished, Tomás closed the café.
yourTurn.answer: Terminado el trabajo, Tomás cerró el café.
yourTurn.why: A participle says the work was already done.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Knowing that Altamira wants to buy, Tomás didn't sign.
yourTurn.answer: Sabiendo que Altamira quiere comprar, Tomás no firmó.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: With the café closed, Vale went home.
yourTurn.answer: Cerrado el café, Vale se fue a casa.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Open since 1950, the café has many customers.
yourTurn.answer: Abierto desde 1950, el café tiene muchos clientes.
yourTurn.why: A participle can describe a state, like *abierto*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Being a foreigner, Tomás didn't know the city.
yourTurn.answer: Siendo extranjero, Tomás no conocía la ciudad.
yourTurn.why: *Siendo* plus a noun or adjective gives a reason about the subject.

pitfalls.wrong: Construida en 1920, el edificio sigue en pie.
pitfalls.right: Construido en 1920, el edificio sigue en pie.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The participle matches *edificio*, so it ends in *-o*.
Almost. A gerund cannot describe something that happens later; use a second verb.

pitfalls.wrong: Terminando el trabajo, Tomás cerró el café.
pitfalls.right: Terminado el trabajo, Tomás cerró el café.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Terminando* means "while finishing"; to say "once finished" use the participle.

pitfalls.wrong: Terminada el trabajo, Tomás cerró el café.
pitfalls.right: Terminado el trabajo, Tomás cerró el café.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Trabajo* is masculine, so the participle ends in *-o*.

personal: Say something true about your day or your city, starting with a participle (*Terminado…*) or *Siendo…*.
